hook_line: You wait weeks for an appointment, then it's over before you know it.

beats.narration: Many doctor visits last around fifteen to twenty minutes, and much of that time goes to paperwork and the exam.
beats.label: Short visits, make them count

beats.narration: Bring your medication list, insurance card, records from other doctors, and a written list of your questions.
beats.label: What to bring

beats.narration: Write down your top three concerns before you go, and say the most worrying one first, not at the door.
beats.label: Say the big one first

beats.narration: Describe symptoms clearly. When did it start, how often does it happen, and how bad is it, one to ten. If you ever have severe symptoms like chest pain, trouble breathing, or sudden weakness, don't wait for an appointment, call 911 or go to the ER right away.
beats.label: Describe symptoms clearly

beats.narration: Try the Ask Me 3 approach: What is my main problem? What do I need to do? Why is it important for me to do this?
beats.label: Ask Me 3

beats.narration: Before you leave, repeat the plan back in your own words. This 'teach-back' method helps catch mix-ups right away, and remember to ask your doctor or pharmacist before stopping or changing any medication on your own. Here's how to make it count.
beats.label: Teach-back method

title: How to Get the Most From a 15-Minute Doctor Visit
